summary: Senarat Wijayasundara works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career includes posts attested in 1999 as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana (1896–1972) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University around 1936–1937.

Senchu Murano (b. 1908) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (until 1933) and the University of Washington (until 1938). He held a professorship at Rissho University, attested in 1972.

Sengaku Mayeda (1931–2026) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at the University of Tokyo and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. He held professorial posts at the University of Tokyo and Musashino University.

Senkyo Sakawa (b. 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. After studying at Rissho University, he served there as professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Senmyo Naniwa (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University and studied under Mohan G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, P. V. Bapat, and Genjun Sasaki, later becoming a professor at Bukkyo University.
Sensho Kimura (b. 1943) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Otani University, where he also held a professorship attested in 2000.

Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Otani and Toyo universities. He served as a lecturer and professor at the University of Tokyo between 1888 and 1923 and held leadership roles at multiple schools.

Seok-hyeong Kim (b. 1904) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University. He held an appointment as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and served as a professor at Dongguk University.

Seong-Uk Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Attested in 2026, he serves as Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University.

Seraphim Rose (1934–1982) was a religious studies and philosophy figure who studied under Alan Watts and attended CIIS and UC Berkeley. From circa 1965 to 1982, he held a post with the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the USA.

Sergey Malov (1880–1957) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies who studied under Nikolai Katanov at Kazan Theological Academy and St. Petersburg University. He held academic posts at Kazan State and Saint Petersburg State universities.

Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934) studied under Ivan Minayev at Saint Petersburg State University, where he became an Indology professor in 1889. He directed the Asiatic Museum and served as Perpetual Secretary of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Serinity Young (1944–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned her PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman. She held posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History in 2000.
Sesso Oda (1901–1966) was an active figure in Buddhist studies who studied under and succeeded Zuigan Goto. His own students included Gary Snyder and Soko Morinaga.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who completed doctoral studies under Lee Sang-hae. Lee has held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2011. Koh has served as an appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Seungsahn Haengwon (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Dongguk University and trained under Kobong Sunim, whom he succeeded in 1957. He founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.

Seán McLoughlin is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who received his PhD from the University of Manchester. Attested in 2005, he served as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds.

Shagun Sinha specializes in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. Sinha earned a PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the doctoral supervision of Girish Nath Jha, attested in 2022, alongside instruction from several other faculty members.
